newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN LENDING RATE DOWN 50 BPS TO 7.8 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN LENDING RATE DOWN 50 BPS TO 7.8 PCT.

text.p: A large volume of call money loans weighed down the Croatian average lending rate 50 basis points to 7.8 percent on Friday, amid high liquidity and low demand.
Daily trade totalled 38.5 million kuna. All fresh borrowings, totalling 33.5 million kuna, were call money deals granted at a steady seven percent.
There were no fresh term loans and some 47 million kuna were left on the supply side.
Banks rolled over old loans at rates varying from 7.0 percent for one-week to 16 and 19 percent for two-month loans.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Saturday and Monday firmed to 6.6517 against the dollar and to 3.5584 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
